Select the OBD Combination of Comb-BOIN12 Trials

Source: R/comb_boin12_select_obd.R
comb_boin12_select_obd.Rd

Select the optimal biological dose combination (OBDC) of one or more trials of the Comb-BOIN12 design of Lu et al. (2025) from their final data. The DLT rates are made monotone along both drugs by bivariate isotonic regression, the maximum tolerated dose combination (MTDC) bounds the candidates, and the OBDC is the admissible candidate with the highest estimated utility.

Usage

comb_boin12_select_obd(
  n_pts,
  n_tox,
  n_resp,
  target,
  target_resp,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  extrasafe = FALSE,
  offset = 0.05,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  est_method = c("logistic", "observed"),
  obd_bound = c("rectangle", "contour"),
  dose_a = NULL,
  dose_b = NULL,
  logistic_scale = c(2.5, 2.5),
  n_draws = 4000,
  early_stop = NULL
)

Arguments

n_pts, n_tox, n_resp

Numeric matrices for a single trial, with one row per level of drug A and one column per level of drug B, or arrays with dimensions trial by level of drug A by level of drug B, of the patients treated, the DLTs and the responses.

target, target_resp, cutoff_eli, cutoff_eli_resp, extrasafe, offset

As in comb_boin12_simulate. The admissibility of the combinations is judged again from the final data with the same rules.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars from 0 to 100. Utilities of a patient with neither a DLT nor a response and with both, as in sim_boin12. Default to 40 and 60.

est_method

Character scalar. Estimate of the response probability: "logistic" (the default) the posterior mean under the logistic model of Lu et al. (2025), see Details; "observed" the observed response rate.

obd_bound

Character scalar. Combinations from which the OBDC is chosen: "rectangle" (the default) those with both levels at most those of the MTDC, as Lu et al. (2025) write; "contour" those, in every column (level of drug B), at most the combination of that column whose isotonic DLT rate is closest to target, the rule that reproduces the results published by Lu et al. (2025). See Details.

dose_a, dose_b

Numeric vectors or NULL. Dose values of the levels of drug A and of drug B in the logistic model. Default to NULL, the level numbers. Each is standardized to mean 0 and standard deviation 0.5.

logistic_scale

Numeric vector of two positive numbers. Scales of the Cauchy priors of the intercept and of the other coefficients of the logistic model. Defaults to c(2.5, 2.5), as in Lu et al. (2025).

n_draws

Integer scalar. Number of points of the importance sampling of the logistic model. Defaults to 4000.

early_stop

Logical vector or NULL. Trials stopped early, which select no OBDC. Defaults to NULL, no trial.

Value

A list with components

obd_a, obd_b

Integer vectors, the levels of drug A and drug B of the OBDC of every trial (NA when none is selected).

mtd_a, mtd_b

Integer vectors, the levels of the MTDC.

reason

Character vector: "selected", "early_stop" or "no_admissible_dose".

tox_est

Array of the isotonic estimates of the DLT rates.

resp_est

Array of the estimates of the response probabilities of the tried combinations (NA elsewhere and for the trials with no selection).

utility

Array of the estimated utilities of the tried combinations, on the scale 0 to 100.

Details

The DLT rates are estimated by (y + 0.05) / (n + 0.1) with weights n + 0.1 and made monotone by Iso::biviso(), as in comb_boin_select_mtd (by Iso::pava() when one drug has a single level). The MTDC is the tried combination whose estimate, plus 1e-5 times the sum of its two levels, is closest to target, the first in column-major order among exact ties: below the target the small amount favors the higher combination, above it the lower one. Untried combinations are never selected.

The utility of a combination is estimated by 100 * pE * (1 - pT) + psi00 * (1 - pT) * (1 - pE) + psi11 * pT * pE, with pT the isotonic estimate and pE the estimate of est_method. When psi00 + psi11 is 100 it is a linear function of pE - wT * pT, the estimated utility of Lu et al. (2025), with wT = psi00 / psi11. The OBDC is the admissible tried candidate with the highest estimate, ties (within 1e-12) to the lowest sum of the levels and then to the first in column-major order.

Lu et al. (2025) state the candidates as the combinations (j, k) with j and k at most the levels of the MTDC. Applied to the trials that reproduce their allocation percentages, that rule gives selection percentages far from those published; obd_bound = "contour", which bounds every level of drug B by its own MTD along drug A, agrees with their Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure S2 (see inst/reproduce/reproduce_Lu2025.R). It treats the two drugs differently.

The logistic model is logit(pE) = g0 + g1 a + g2 b + g3 a^2 + g4 b^2, with a and b the standardized doses (mean 0 and standard deviation 0.5 over the levels of each drug, the scaling of Gelman et al., 2008, for these priors; Lu et al., 2025, do not state one) and independent Cauchy priors centered at 0. Lu et al. draw the posterior with Gibbs sampling; here its mean is computed by importance sampling with n_draws Halton points: the proposal is a multivariate t distribution with 4 degrees of freedom centered at the posterior mode, with the inverse of the negative Hessian as scale matrix, and it is fitted twice more to the weighted mean and covariance of the weighted points. No random number is used, so that the selection does not change the random number stream. In checks against long Markov chain Monte Carlo runs the estimates were within 0.01.

References

Lu, M., Zhang, J., Yuan, Y. and Lin, R. (2025). Comb-BOIN12: A utility-based Bayesian optimal interval design for dose optimization in cancer drug-combination trials. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research, 17(2), 266-276. doi:10.1080/19466315.2024.2370403

Gelman, A., Jakulin, A., Pittau, M. G. and Su, Y.-S. (2008). A weakly informative default prior distribution for logistic and other regression models. The Annals of Applied Statistics, 2(4), 1360-1383. doi:10.1214/08-AOAS191

See also

sim_comb_boin12, comb_boin12_simulate

Examples

n_pts <- matrix(c(3, 6, 0, 9, 12, 3), nrow = 2)
n_tox <- matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 1), nrow = 2)
n_resp <- matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 3, 6, 2), nrow = 2)
comb_boin12_select_obd(n_pts, n_tox, n_resp, target = 0.33,
                       target_resp = 0.2)
